summary: Intermittent 502s and stalled model artifact downloads due to HTTP/2 stream window inversion caused by WAN optimizer egress path
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 502 errors from the control plane and stalled model artifact downloads on their private deployment. Failures coincide with long-lived gRPC/HTTP2 connections used for artifact retrieval and serving node KV sync.

Impact:
- Artifact downloads (presigned URL -> S3 behind their egress path) fail with 502/ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR roughly every 15-30 minutes for a subset (~6%) of requests.
- Long-lived gRPC streams to serving nodes pause for 10–60s then recover, causing request latency spikes and several downstream user-facing errors.
- Affects production workloads for Neptune Analytics' private VPC deployment in us-west-2; customer reports increased error budget burn and consumer impact.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC peering -> customer on-prem MPLS -> WAN optimizer -> internet egress)
- Redwood control-plane + serving nodes in us-west-2 (prod)
- TLS: mutual TLS to control plane, ALPN h2 enabled for artifact fetches and gRPC traffic

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger a model artifact download (large model shard ~350MB) via private deployment artifact fetch flow.
2) Open long-lived streaming session against serving nodes (simulate sustained inference with keepalive=15s).
3) Observe occasional 502/HTTP2 protocol errors and pauses in streaming throughput after ~10-30 minutes.

Observed behavior / logs:
- Control plane logs show repeated HTTP2_ERROR (PROTOCOL_ERROR) and RST_STREAM events during artifact GETs.
- Serving runtime metrics show periods of stalled outbound bytes and increased retransmits on TCP layer reported by the kernel.
- Packet captures (pcap from customer egress appliance) show out-of-order segments and reordered HTTP/2 WINDOW_UPDATE frames where the window sequence appears inverted relative to stream data.
- WAN optimizer (third-party device) logs indicate aggressive re-segmentation and L7 buffering under bursts.

Investigation notes / hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: WAN optimizer is reassembling/re-segmenting and replaying HTTP/2 frames in a way that inverts WINDOW_UPDATE ordering causing the receiver to enforce a protocol error.
- Hypothesis B: Intermediate box performs TCP-level rewriting (zero-window or MSS clamping) and triggers reordering leading to HTTP/2 flow control inversion.
- Hypothesis C: Path MTU/MSS and on-path buffering combine with parallel TCP sessions and selective ACKs causing TCP-level reordering large enough to violate expected HTTP/2 stream window semantics.

Evidence collected so far:
- PCAPs correlate customer-side reordering with time of observed 502s.
- Replaying packets in a lab (with a WAN optimizer in the path) reproduces the HTTP/2 WINDOW_UPDATE inversion and RST_STREAM.
- Metrics show increased kernel retransmits and occasional dup-ACK spikes during incidents.

Temporary mitigations and workarounds:
- Customer disabled WAN optimizer HTTP/2/L7 acceleration mode last night and reported a drop in error rate (preliminary).
- Suggested temporary policy: route artifact downloads via an alternate egress path that bypasses the appliance (customer tested via split-eDNS and reported lower failure rate).

Next steps / action items:
- SRE: request full pcap for the failing time window and share a sanitized excerpt with runtime team (actioned).
- Networking: validate MSS/MTU settings across customer transit and ensure no clamping below 1280.
- Runtime: add additional defensive handling for out-of-order WINDOW_UPDATE sequences in the artifact-fetch HTTP2 client to avoid immediate RST_STREAM on borderline cases (low-risk patch candidate).
- Customer-facing: coordinate a maintenance window with Neptune to temporarily bypass the WAN optimizer for a 24h validation window.

Resolution: ongoing. Temporary bypass appears to reduce occurrences; root cause likely due to WAN optimizer re-sequencing HTTP/2 frames. Permanent remediation requires either appliance configuration change or runtime tolerance improvements.
investigation_notes: PCAP replay in lab reproduced WINDOW_UPDATE inversion when WAN optimizer L7 acceleration and TCP re-segmentation enabled. Kernel tcp_info shows out-of-order packets count rising with bursts. Reproduced with two different vendor appliances (ApplianceX v3.2, ApplianceY v2.9) in lab under acceleration mode. Patch proposal: guard in HTTP2 client to queue WINDOW_UPDATE adjustments if sequence appears decreasing within a narrow timing window, rather than immediate protocol error. Networking recommendation: disable HTTP/2 L7 acceleration on appliance or reduce re-segmentation and ensure SACK + window scaling preserved end-to-end.
resolution: In progress — customer has temporarily bypassed the WAN optimizer for artifact fetches and reported ~90% reduction in observed 502s. Runtime patch PR drafted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8421 (adds defensive window-update handling and more verbose debug logs). Coordinating with customer to test patch in staging prior to production rollout. Final resolution pending appliance config change or runtime release.
